subject: Request: regional SLA carveouts, transient handoff windows & subprocessor roster
messages:
From: Samantha Walker <samantha.walker@medlumen.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@medlumen.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Residency commitments + temporary egress window question

Hi Jasmine,

We're working through the DPA review with our legal and security teams and had two specific asks before we proceed:

1) Can Redwood commit to EU-only processing for MedLumen production traffic, with transient handoff windows only allowed under documented incident or migration scenarios? Our security team understands short-lived operational exceptions may be necessary, but they want an explicit maximum window (hours), notification SLA, and telemetry retention specifics.

2) We also need the current subprocessor roster and an explanation of the policy that governs temporary cross-region processing (what triggers it, who approves, how customers are notified).

I've attached a draft DPA with our proposed redlines and a CSV that lists subprocessors we expect to reconcile. Can you confirm whether these requests are acceptable and, if not, provide proposed language and SLAs we can evaluate?

Thanks — we have a gated procurement timeline (vendor selection by 09/10).

Best,
Samantha Walker\Director of IT Security\MedLumen Health

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Samantha Walker <samantha.walker@medlumen.com>
Cc: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@medlumen.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency commitments + temporary egress window question

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear asks and the redlines. Quick answers up front: yes, we support EU-only pinned processing in production for accounts that require it; we also have a documented temporary egress/failover policy for operational events.

I'll summarize the key commitments and attach a short runbook for the types of events that can trigger temporary routing:
- EU pinned: We can designate your tenant to the eu-region pool with strict routing and storage locality for live inference traffic and telemetry.
- Temporary handoff: Allowed only for (a) emergency incident response where site availability is impacted, (b) scheduled disaster-recovery drills if pre-authorized, or (c) customer-requested migrations.
- Max transient window: default 72 hours, with a shorter 24-hour window available under negotiated SLA (we can propose 24/72 tiers in the DPA).
- Notification SLA: 4 hours initial notification to the customer's security contact plus a post-incident report within 5 business days.
- Telemetry retention during transient processing: logs and traces created during the window are retained per your retention policy; copies will remain within the EU control plane unless explicit cross-border KMS rotation is requested.

To make sure we capture legally-sufficient language, I'm looping in Marissa (privacy counsel) and Ben (security operations) to propose DPA text and provide the current subprocessor roster and a short description of approval flows. Kar (ops) will confirm the operational runbook and the mechanics for limiting window length.

Can you confirm the contacts who should receive the 4-hour notifications and whether MedLumen will accept the default 72-hour transient maximum or require the 24-hour tier?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu\Account Lead, Enterprise\Redwood Inference

---

From: Samantha Walker <samantha.walker@medlumen.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@medlumen.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency commitments + temporary egress window question

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Two clarifications from our side:

- Notification contacts: SecurityOps@medlumen.com (primary) and Legal@medlumen.com (secondary). Please make initial notice to the SecurityOps alias.
- We prefer the 24-hour transient maximum if Redwood can guarantee the operational safeguards (automated routing rollback and preauth controls). If 24 hours is problematic, we will need written justification and a compensating control (e.g., real-time audit stream to our SIEM while the window is open).

Also, Marissa (once onboarded to this thread) and our procurement lead would like a CSV of the current subprocessor roster and a short note on whether any subprocessors are in jurisdictions outside the EU/UK and the typical contractual controls for those subprocessors.

Appreciate it — procurement timeline still 09/10.

Best,
Samantha

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Walker <samantha.walker@medlumen.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency commitments + temporary egress window question

Hi Samantha — Marissa from Legal here. Appreciate the specificity; a few concrete items attached and a proposed redline for the DPA sections you flagged. Summary below: 

1) EU-only processing: we can include a tenancy-level residency clause that requires primary inference and data-at-rest for production requests to remain in the EU. We've proposed language that allows transient egress only for three enumerated cases (incident response, pre-authorized migration, scheduled DR) and requires prior technical approval for any other scenario.

2) Maximum transient window: we can offer a standard 72-hour maximum. We can also offer a 24-hour maximum as a premium SLA addendum; this requires an operational runbook and additional monitoring (we'll include an addendum with automated rollback triggers and a real-time audit feed to your SIEM as a contractual control). Pricing/SLAs to be included in the commercial schedule.

3) Notification and evidence: initial notification within 4 hours (as Jasmine noted). Post-event report within 5 business days; we will include a snapshot of telemetry metadata. For the 24-hour tier we recommend continuous audit streaming to your SIEM (we can send a sample event schema).

4) Subprocessors: attached is the current roster (CSV). A few notes: some cloud infra subprocessors operate global control planes but we contractually limit processing for pinned tenants; any subprocessor outside the EU is bound by our DPA flow-downs and SCCs where applicable. If MedLumen needs full on-prem or air-gapped options we can discuss Private deployment terms.

Next steps: please review the attached redline (DPA_redlines_MedLumen_v1_legalredline.docx) and the subprocessor roster. If you confirm the 24-hour premium request we will produce the SLA addendum and an ops checklist for Kar to sign-off on. Would you be able to confirm early next week so we can lock procurement timing?

Best regards,
Marissa Cole\Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance\Redwood Inference
